extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, auditors and accounting firms, securities lawyers and compliance officers, PCAOB and other standard-setters
extracted.subtask_description: Subsidiary extraction of the SEC's final-rule guidance on where and how climate-related financial statement metrics must be disclosed, audited, and phased into existing forms (e.g., Form 10-K, 20-F), including scope, exemptions, materiality, and related PCAOB auditing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of financial statement effects disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that the financial statement effects disclosure be presented in a note to the financial statements (Rule 14-01(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying a specific location—a note to the financial statements—will make the information more accessible to investors; the disclosures present financial information derived from registrants' books and records and consistent presentation in notes aligns them with other financial statement disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjecting disclosures to financial-statement audit and ICFR
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures included in the financial statements shall be subject to a financial statement audit and registrants' internal control over financial reporting (ICFR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjecting the disclosures to audit and ICFR enhances reliability; the Commission does not exempt these disclosures from audit or ICFR because doing so could confuse investors about which parts of the financial statements are covered by audit and ICFR. Phase-in periods are intended to give registrants/auditors time to familiarize themselves with new requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on treating the metrics as unaudited supplemental information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission considered but rejected providing the financial statement disclosures as supplemental information or schedules outside the financial statements; instead they must be in a financial statement note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although commenters recommended supplemental schedules or separate reports, the Commission concluded the information is derived from books and records already in the statements and should therefore be in the notes to enhance accessibility and usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of PCAOB auditing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PCAOB auditing standards can and will apply to the financial statement disclosures included in a note to the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission expects existing PCAOB standards to be applicable and that auditors will incorporate procedures to audit these note disclosures into their current audits; the Commission will work with the PCAOB to address issues and consider issuing additional guidance if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality application and one-percent threshold considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors should apply PCAOB AS 2105 (Consideration of Materiality in Planning and Performing an Audit) and related materiality concepts when assessing the proposed disclosure threshold (e.g., the proposed one percent disclosure threshold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors must remain alert for misstatements that could be material for quantitative or qualitative reasons; if particular accounts/disclosures are susceptible to misstatements of lesser amounts, auditors should establish separate materiality levels to plan audit procedures. Numerous GAAP/Regulation S-X rules include percentage thresholds and auditors have procedures for auditing such disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for additional PCAOB guidance and inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional guidance from the PCAOB may be necessary to address the application of auditing standards to these climate-related financial statement metrics, and the PCAOB should consider inspection focus on this issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters requested specific guidance (including on particular PCAOB standards); the Commission noted it will work with the PCAOB to address auditing issues and may consider issuing guidance to the extent needed and helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of auditor specialists and auditor-engaged specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors may use the work of auditor-employed or auditor-engaged specialists if appropriate under PCAOB standards (e.g., AS 2101, AS 1201, AS 1210).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AS 2101 para .16 indicates auditors should determine whether specialized skill/knowledge is needed; when using specialists, auditors must consider supervision (AS 1201) and the use of auditor-engaged specialists (AS 1210) as appropriate; this does not permit replacing the auditor with non-PCAOB registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may issue audit opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission expects PCAOB-registered public accounting firms to perform the audit and issue audit opinions on the financial statements (including the new climate-related note).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The auditor's unqualified opinion covers the financial statements and related notes; while auditors can use specialists' work, the audit and opinion are issued by PCAOB-registered firms subject to PCAOB inspection and quality-control requirements. The Commission rejected allowing sustainability consultants outside the traditional accounting sector to be the auditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and basis of presentation for IFRS filers and Form 20-F
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that the financial statement disclosure requirements must be included in the scope of the audit when a registrant files financial statements prepared in accordance with IFRS as issued by the IASB, and that the rules will not alter the basis of presentation of financial statements as referred to in an auditor's report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions to Form 20-F require that foreign issuer financial statements be audited in accordance with PCAOB standards; PCAOB AS 3101.08 supports including notes within the scope of the auditor’s report when noted as audited financial statements and related notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of registrants required to provide climate-related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the climate-related disclosure rules to registrants with Exchange Act reporting obligations under Exchange Act section 13(a) or 15(d) and companies filing Securities Act or Exchange Act registration statements; require disclosures in Forms S-1, F-1, S-3, F-3, S-4, F-4, S-11, Forms 10 and 20-F, and Exchange Act annual reports (Forms 10-K and 20-F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to other important business/financial information, the Commission proposed and largely adopted inclusion across registration statements and annual reports; commenters debated scope for certain categories of filers (SRCs, EGCs, BDCs, MJDS filers, asset-backed issuers, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of smaller reporting companies (SRCs) and Scope 3 emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: SRCs were proposed to be exempted from the Scope 3 emissions disclosure requirement (but otherwise subject to most proposed rules); commenters debated exemptions and phase-in accommodations for SRCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters urged exemption or longer phase-ins for SRCs citing disproportionate compliance burden; others opposed indefinite exemptions. Commission considered comments and phase-in timing when finalizing scope for SRCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of emerging growth companies (EGCs) and newly public companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters recommended exempting or phasing in EGCs and newly public companies; some suggested phase-in until the end of the first full fiscal year after going public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Views varied: some urged exemptions (to avoid deterring IPOs), others recommended longer phase-ins rather than full exemption; the Commission solicited comment and considered scaling/delaying compliance for EGCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign private issuers, MJDS filers, and alternative reporting regimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters supported requiring foreign private issuers to provide the same disclosures as domestic registrants; others urged allowing foreign private issuers to follow their home jurisdiction or alternative reporting regimes to avoid duplicative requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission clarified that the disclosures must be in scope when filing under IFRS and noted MJDS filers were proposed to be excluded given comparable home-jurisdiction regimes (e.g., Canadian CSA proposal modeled on TCFD); commenters recommended deferral until counterpart frameworks are finalized or found substantially similar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions for certain issuer types (asset-backed issuers, BDCs, REITs, pooled vehicles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rules would not apply to asset-backed issuers and commenters suggested excluding BDCs, certain registered collective investment vehicles, REITs, exchange-traded products, and issuers of non-variable insurance contracts given their different structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued disclosures for many of these vehicles are inappropriate or require a different tailored framework (e.g., ABS Climate Disclosure Framework for asset-backed issuers). The Commission solicited comment on these exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim/updating requirement for material changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Require registrants to disclose any material change to the climate-related disclosures provided in a registration statement or annual report in their Form 10-Q (or, in certain circumstances, Form 6-K for foreign private issuers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters supported quarterly updating because climate risks are financial risks; others opposed interim updates, arguing climate metrics are long-term in nature and that quarterly updates would impose costs and provide limited incremental value. The Commission solicited comment and considered these views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in periods and transition approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide phase-in periods for compliance to give registrants and their auditors time to familiarize themselves with new requirements and to mitigate implementation burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters suggested initially including financial statement metrics outside the statements with a later transition into the financial statements; the final rules narrowed scope and provided phase-ins to ease burdens and audit readiness concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost considerations and audit-fee impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize commenters' concerns that audit and ICFR assessments for the metrics could result in significant costs and increased audit fees, but the Commission expects modest audit-cost increases for most companies given the narrower final scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters provided estimates of audit costs and warned of increased fees depending on granularity, complexity, and need for specialists; the Commission noted costs may decrease or stabilize over time as audit practices mature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for forward-looking or other climate-related financial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters requested a safe harbor (both limited to forward-looking items and broader); the Commission concluded a safe harbor is not necessary or appropriate for the narrowed financial statement disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters argued a safe harbor would protect registrants given the estimates/judgments involved; the Commission rejected adopting a safe harbor because narrowing scope and focusing on amounts derived from books and records and material estimates reduces the complexities prompting such requests.
